catalog_quote: 4.3 Vowel length. Bungu does not have contrastive stem-internal vowel length, but some vowel length can be heard and measured in certain positions. Labroussi suggests that vowel length in Bungu is “mostly dependent on emphasis and a careful vs. fast articulation…” (1999:360), however vowel length can be morphologically contrastive in Bungu. ... 4.3.1 Vowel length in the penultimate syllable. This vowel length is conditioned rather than contrastive, and occurs in all multisyllabic words. Phonetically, the vowel can be up to two and a half times as long as a vowel in the anti-penultimate syllable. If the vowel follows a labialised or palatalised consonant, or precedes a prenasalised consonant, there is no additional lengthening of the vowel (see section 4.3.2 for the exception to this). [pp. 32-33] ... 6.1 Generalities. The tone bearing unit (TBU) in Bungu is analysed as the mora rather than the syllable, and all phonetically long vowels are analysed as consisting of two mora. This analysis is motivated by the presence of rising and falling tones on phonetically long syllables, contrastive to level highs. For example, kolɔ̂la ‘to look’ and kokówa ‘to fall’ have a falling tone and level high tone, respectively, on the penultimate (PU) syllable. ... Bungu high tones are subject to downstep. [p. 40]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bungu is described as a tone language (lexical and grammatical tone, mora as TBU); the description never uses the terms 'stress' or 'accent'. The only word-level prominence cue reported is automatic, non-contrastive lengthening of the penultimate syllable of every multisyllabic word (measured at up to 2.5x the antepenult vowel), the usual Bantu penultimate-prominence pattern; lengthening is suppressed after labialised/palatalised consonants and before prenasalised consonants. If this penultimate lengthening is taken as the stress correlate, the reading would be fixed: penultimate syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: No penultimate lengthening when the penult vowel follows a labialised or palatalised consonant or precedes a prenasalised consonant (p. 32-33, with §4.3.2 exceptions); phrase-final words with a final high tone get boundary-L insertion and final-vowel lengthening instead (§4.3.4, p. 35). Gray also quotes Labroussi (1999:360) that vowel length in Bungu is 'mostly dependent on emphasis and a careful vs. fast articulation', which she rejects for morphological length.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: 'all multisyllabic words' (verbs and nouns in citation form, measured in recordings of isolated words, Table 22 p. 33); the final-vowel lengthening in §4.3.4 is explicitly phrase-final.
new_statements.identity_note: Gray 2020 describes the Bungu of the villages east of Lake Rukwa (Mwambani, Maleza, Udinde, Manda A consultants; p. 3), i.e. Glottolog bung1265 proper; the survey (Smith et al. 2008) treats the Gua/Manda variety as possibly Kimbu-related, and Gray excludes it. No dialect issue for the stress/length statement.
